subject: Storify SLA: baseline uptime & monthly credit structure
messages:
From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@storify.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@storify.com
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Storify SLA request: baseline uptime & credit cap

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the demo last week — product looked promising. Legal/ops asked me to share a draft of the SLA items they're most focused on so we can converge quickly:

- Baseline uptime: Storify expects 99.95% or better for production endpoints.
- Monthly remedy: credits should be capped at 15% of the monthly invoice (Storify prefers lower).
- Maintenance: any maintenance >30 minutes should be notified 7 days in advance; emergency maintenance needs post-mortem within 48 hours.
- Pro rata: if we start mid-month, remedies should be pro-rated.
- On-call: for Sev-1 incidents impacting revenue >1 hour, we ask for a named on-call contact and 1-hour acknowledgement SLA.

I've attached a short PDF with the items (Storify_SLA_Request.pdf) and our procurement redlines (Redlines_Storify_SLA.docx).

Can you confirm Redwood's standard position and any flexibility on the remedy cap (we'd like to avoid a large one-off credit that destabilizes our month).

Best,
Elliot

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Storify SLA request: baseline uptime & credit cap

Hi Elliot — thanks for sending this over and for the clear list. We've had internal alignment and I wanted to surface our starting position so we can iterate: 

- Baseline uptime: Redwood standard for hosted production is 99.90% (monthly). For customers sizing predictable capacity we offer 99.95% as a dedicated option; there is a commitment delta and pricing difference.
- Monthly remedy cap: our default is 10% of the monthly invoice (calculated on billed service for the month).
- Maintenance notification: we provide a 7-day notice for planned maintenance; emergency maintenance is rare and accompanied by a post-mortem within 72 hours (we can accelerate to 48h on request).
- Pro rata: remedies are pro-rated for partial months on a daily basis.
- On-call: we include a named escalation contact for Sev-1 incidents with a 1-hour acknowledgement for customers on Dedicated; for Hosted customers we commit to a 4-hour acknowledgement and triage cadence unless on a support addendum.

Two proposals to bridge the gap and avoid a large one-off credit: 
1) Remedy escrow pool: Redwood can offer an optional monthly remedy escrow — we allocate a small percentage of the monthly recurring bill into an escrow pool that smooths out heavy one-off credits. Unused escrow carries forward for up to three months.
2) Tiered cap: keep a 10% monthly cap but allow a quarterly reconciliation where, if Storify experiences repeated deficits, we can discuss a one-time supplementary credit (capped annually) to address systemic issues.

I've attached our Redwood_SLA_Template_v4.pdf for your legal team to review. Happy to hop on a short call to walk through the escrow flow if that helps.

Best,
Olga

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Storify SLA request: baseline uptime & credit cap

Folks — quick note from pricing ops: Storify is in a mid-sized tier and currently running latency-sensitive inference. If we offer 99.95% for their production endpoints we should:

- Require a 3-month minimum commitment and a small uplift (we can price this alongside Dedicated capacity).
- Include the remedy escrow as an opt-in line item with an initial allocation of 2% of monthly bill that can be increased if they prefer more buffer.

The escrow eases procurement concerns about lump-sum credits and is an easy legal addendum rather than a permanent change to credit architecture.

Ben

--
Ben Carter
Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@storify.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Jasmine Turner <jasmine.turner@storify.com>, contracts@storify.com
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 11:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Storify SLA request: baseline uptime & credit cap

Thanks Olga — helpful summary. A few clarifications and a counter-proposal from Storify: 

- Baseline: Storify can accept 99.90% for hosted if Redwood commits to a 1-hour incident acknowledgment for Sev-1 (we need timely triage).
- Remedy cap: we are willing to move toward 10% monthly cap if the remedy escrow is in place, but we'd like the escrow allocation to be visible on the invoice and refundable if not used after a 3-month pilot.
- Maintenance: 7-day notice is fine; for emergency maintenance we still need a 48-hour post-mortem.
- Pilot: propose a 3-month pilot (start of production month counts as month 1) where the escrow pool is 3% and is refundable if not used during pilot; after pilot we evaluate whether to keep escrow or move to standard 2% opt-in.

Attached: Redlines_Storify_SLA.docx with specific marked clauses.

Would Redwood consider the 3-month refundable pilot escrow + 10% cap if we accept 99.90% hosted baseline?

Cheers,
Elliot

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot.price@storify.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Storify SLA request: baseline uptime & credit cap

Elliot — appreciate the thoughtful counter-proposal and the marked redlines. Summary of agreed points and next steps so we're aligned: 

Agreed (Redwood willingness):
- Baseline uptime: 99.90% for Hosted production (no change in product flow). Dedicated 99.95% is available with a 3-month minimum commitment and published capacity uplift.
- Monthly remedy cap: 10% of monthly invoice (standard).
- Remedy escrow pilot: we will run a 3-month refundable escrow pilot at 3% of monthly recurring service. The escrow will be visible as a separate line on the invoice and refundable at pilot close if not used to offset remedies. Escrow carries forward month-to-month during the pilot only.
- Incident acknowledgement: Redwood will provide a named escalation contact and commit to a 1-hour acknowledgement for Sev-1 incidents during the pilot. After pilot, acknowledgement window for Hosted customers reverts to standard 4 hours unless an addendum is signed.
- Maintenance: Redwood will aim for a 48-hour post-mortem for emergency maintenance during the pilot and 7 days advance notice for planned maintenance.

Open items / legal redlines to resolve:
- Exact wording for escrow refundable conditions (Laura/legal to pick language).
- Definition of "Sev-1" impact threshold — Storify proposes "customer-reported production outage impacting >25% of requests or revenue-critical endpoints"; Redwood legal to propose an alternative.
- Billing mechanics for pro rata on mid-month starts (we do daily proration; will include formula).

Next steps:
1) Laura, can your team draft the short SLA addendum reflecting the pilot escrow language and Sev-1 definition? (see Drive link above for template).
2) Ben, please prepare a pricing sheet showing the Dedicated 99.95% uplift and the 3% escrow allocation on a sample monthly invoice.
3) Elliot/Jasmine, if you can confirm acceptance of the above we will circulate a DocuSign addendum for signatures and schedule the pilot start for the first business day after signature.

If agreeable, I'll also include the SLA_Support_Addendum.pdf as the one-page operational escalation we mentioned.

Thanks — I think this is a practical compromise that keeps Storify protected without creating a large one-off liability for Redwood.

Best,
Olga
